readerTitle: The remodeler who said yes to every estimate
caseNote: 가상 사례 (주방 리모델링 업체, 금속 부품 가공 공장) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 자격 확인은 고객을 거르는 일이 아니라, 살 수 있는 고객에게 시간을 몰아주는 일이다.
misconception: 문의는 전부 잠재 매출이니, 모든 요청에 최대한 빨리 견적을 내 주는 것이 좋은 영업이다.

sources.text: 영업의 표준 개념 (리드 자격 확인: 필요, 예산, 결정권자, 시기)

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 첫 시즌: 방문 견적 30건 × 4시간 = 120시간, 수주 6건, 수주 1건당 120 ÷ 6 = 20시간.
둘째 시즌: 전화 30통 × 5분 = 2.5시간, 방문 15건 × 4시간 = 60시간, 합계 62.5시간, 수주 6건, 수주 1건당 62.5 ÷ 6 ≈ 10.4시간. 수주 건수가 같다는 것은 설명용 가정입니다.
BANT(Budget, Authority, Need, Timing)는 널리 쓰이는 영업 체크리스트 이름입니다. 기원(IBM 등)에 대한 주장은 카드에 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: The remodeler who said yes to every estimate
body: Dana runs a small kitchen remodeling business. One spring, she drove to 30 homes to give free estimates. Each one took about four hours: travel, measuring, pricing, writing it up.
She won six jobs. Her calendar was full. Her bank account was not.

image.label: A tired contractor's car full of tape measures and quote folders
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 밴 조수석에 견적서 폴더가 산처럼 쌓여 있고, 지도 앱 화면에 핀이 30개 찍혀 있음. 그중 6개만 초록색. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: A new request comes in.
body: A caller says: "We're thinking about redoing the whole kitchen. Can you come give us a price?"
Dana's week is already busy. What should she do first?

options.text: Book a home visit right away, before they call someone else
options.feedback: Speed can win jobs, but she commits four hours before knowing if this buyer is ready, able or even the one who decides.

options.text: Ask a few short questions on the phone first: when, rough budget, who decides
options.feedback: Five minutes tells her whether the visit is worth four hours. Serious buyers usually welcome the questions.

options.text: Email a price list and let them come back if interested
options.feedback: It protects her time, but she learns nothing, and serious buyers may feel brushed off and go elsewhere.

cards.title: Where the spring went.
body: Looking back, most lost estimates weren't lost to rivals. Some people were planning for next year. Some had a budget far below a full remodel. Some needed a landlord or partner who never saw the quote.

cards.title: Qualifying
body: **Qualifying** means checking early whether a prospect can and will buy, so you spend your time where a sale is possible.
It usually comes down to four things: a real need, the money to pay, the power to decide, and a reason to act soon. Sales teams sometimes call this checklist BANT: budget, authority, need, timing.
Dana's problem wasn't her estimates. It was that she gave her best effort before asking any of these.

image.label: Four gates a lead passes through: need, money, decision, timing
image.brief: 깔때기 대신 작은 문 4개가 일렬로 있는 일러스트. 각 문에 "Need", "Money", "Who decides", "When" 라벨. 사람 모양 아이콘 여러 개가 들어가고 마지막 문을 통과한 몇 명만 집 모양 목적지에 도착.

cards.title: Five minutes on the phone, half the hours.
body: The next spring, Dana asked three questions on every call: When do you want this done? What range are you thinking? Who else needs to agree?
She visited half as many homes and won the same six jobs.

cards.title: A clear "not yet" helps the customer too.
body: Qualifying isn't only about protecting your time. A family with half the budget for a full remodel is better served by hearing that early, and maybe getting a smaller option or a referral.
The same check works anywhere effort comes before the sale: a caterer's tasting, an accountant's free review, a wholesaler's samples.
cards.softwareNote: Demo requests and trial sign-ups are leads too. A question or two on the form, such as team size or timeline, lets a software company send small accounts to self-serve and give sales calls to buyers who can actually decide.

cards.title: Qualify, don't interrogate.
body: Many customers don't know their budget yet. Offer a range, such as "most kitchens we do land between X and Y," instead of demanding a number.
And "not now" is not "never." Someone planning for next year is a future customer. Keep a short list and follow up later.
Strict rules can also screen out good buyers who just answer badly on a first call.

image.label: A notebook with a 'Later' list of names and months
image.brief: 손글씨 노트 한 페이지. 제목 "Later", 아래에 이름과 월(예: "Kim, March", "Lee, after move")이 적혀 있고 옆에 달력 아이콘. 따뜻한 색감.

cards.title: Now it's a machine shop.
body: You run a small metal parts shop. A large manufacturer emails a drawing and asks for a quote on 10,000 parts, needed next month. Pricing it properly takes your engineer two days.

options.text: Quote it right away. A big name could change the business
options.feedback: Two days of engineering go out before you know if they're just collecting prices to pressure their current supplier.

options.text: Decline. Big firms rarely switch suppliers
options.feedback: You keep the two days, but you may walk away from a real order without ever checking.

options.text: Call the buyer first: why they're quoting, how many shops are bidding, who approves, and whether next month is firm
options.feedback: A short call shows whether this is a real chance worth two days, or a price check you can answer roughly.

cards.title: Check fit before you give your best effort.
body: Every lead costs time. Qualifying makes sure that time goes to people with a need, the money, the power to decide and a reason to act soon.
**Try it today:** write the three questions you'll ask before your next estimate, quote or demo.
